speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. To begin our evaluation of your longstanding pruritic rash and the numbness or tingling in your palms, please describe the specific appearance of the rash and its distribution. REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count, Comprehensive Metabolic Panel, ESR.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the normal labs; since the rash has been longstanding and is accompanied by numbness and tingling in your palms, I need to know exactly where the rash is located and what triggers the sensation changes. REQUEST IMAGES: Palpation of skin lesions, sensation mapping.

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of an itchy rash on his upper body and face. Additionally, he has been experiencing a numbness and tingling sensation on both palms. He has been working on his family's rice farm, also caring for livestock.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; the combination of a pruritic rash on the upper body and face, along with numbness in the palms, while working on a rice farm and caring for livestock, strongly suggests a specific parasitic infestation. Can you confirm if you have noticed any small, raised, thread-like larvae under your skin, or if the sensation changes when you touch the rash? REQUEST TEST: Serology for Strongyloides stercoralis and Toxocara.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal serology for Strongyloides and Toxocara makes a primary parasitic infestation less likely, despite your farming history. Given your occupation with livestock and the specific combination of a chronic pruritic rash and symmetric hand paresthesias, could you clarify if the rash resembles the "ground itch" of hookworms or if you have noticed any other skin findings? REQUEST TEST: Eosinophil Count, Peripheral Blood Smear.
